title: T04 What Does an Exchange Do?

lines.text: Lesson four: what does an exchange do? Let's look inside the marketplace.
lines.say: Lesson four: what does an exchange do? Let's look inside the marketplace.

lines.text: An exchange is a business that runs a marketplace where people buy and sell assets.
lines.say: An exchange is a business that runs a marketplace where people buy and sell assets.

lines.text: Like a big market hall: it brings buyers and sellers together, and keeps the record.
lines.say: Like a big market hall: it brings buyers and sellers together, and keeps the record.

lines.text: A trading platform is the app or website you use to reach it.
lines.say: A trading platform is the app or website you use to reach it.

lines.text: An order is an instruction: buy or sell, how much, and at what price.
lines.say: An order is an instruction: buy or sell, how much, and at what price.

lines.text: This one says: buy 0.01 BTC at 60,000 USDT. That's 600 USDT in total.
lines.say: This one says: buy zero point zero one B-T-C at sixty thousand U-S-D-T. That's six hundred U-S-D-T in total.

lines.text: If nobody sells at that price yet, the order waits in a list.
lines.say: If nobody sells at that price yet, the order waits in a list.

lines.text: The order book is a live list of waiting orders, sorted by price.
lines.say: The order book is a live list of waiting orders, sorted by price.

lines.text: Sell orders sit on top. The cheapest one is closest to the middle.
lines.say: Sell orders sit on top. The cheapest one is closest to the middle.

lines.text: Buy orders sit below. The highest one is closest to the middle.
lines.say: Buy orders sit below. The highest one is closest to the middle.

lines.text: New orders keep arriving and leaving, so the book changes all the time.
lines.say: New orders keep arriving and leaving, so the book changes all the time.

lines.text: Two prices matter most. The bid is the highest price a buyer is waiting to pay.
lines.say: Two prices matter most. The bid is the highest price a buyer is waiting to pay.

lines.text: The ask is the lowest price a seller is waiting to accept.
lines.say: The ask is the lowest price a seller is waiting to accept.

lines.text: Here the bid is 59,990 USDT, and the ask is 60,010 USDT.
lines.say: Here the bid is fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety U-S-D-T, and the ask is sixty thousand ten U-S-D-T.

lines.text: The spread is the gap between them: the ask minus the bid.
lines.say: The spread is the gap between them: the ask minus the bid.

lines.text: 60,010 minus 59,990 is a spread of 20 USDT.
lines.say: Sixty thousand ten minus fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety is a spread of twenty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Now a new buyer offers 60,000. The best bid moves up, and the spread shrinks to 10.
lines.say: Now a new buyer offers sixty thousand. The best bid moves up, and the spread shrinks to ten.

lines.text: In a quiet market with few orders, the spread is often wider.
lines.say: In a quiet market with few orders, the spread is often wider.

lines.text: Matching: the exchange pairs orders whose prices meet.
lines.say: Matching: the exchange pairs orders whose prices meet.

lines.text: A buyer wants 0.30 BTC and will pay up to 60,020 USDT.
lines.say: A buyer wants zero point three B-T-C and will pay up to sixty thousand twenty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: First, 0.20 BTC fills at the best ask, 60,010.
lines.say: First, zero point two B-T-C fills at the best ask, sixty thousand ten.

lines.text: The other 0.10 BTC fills at the next ask, 60,020.
lines.say: The other zero point one B-T-C fills at the next ask, sixty thousand twenty.

lines.text: Total: 0.30 BTC for 18,004 USDT. The last trade price is now 60,020.
lines.say: Total: zero point three B-T-C for eighteen thousand four U-S-D-T. The last trade price is now sixty thousand twenty.

lines.text: Your turn. A buyer wants 0.10 BTC, paying up to 60,015 USDT. Which sell orders fill it?
lines.say: Your turn. A buyer wants zero point one B-T-C, paying up to sixty thousand fifteen U-S-D-T. Which sell orders fill it?

lines.text: 0.05 BTC at 60,010, then 0.05 BTC at 60,015. The 60,030 order is above the limit.
lines.say: Zero point zero five B-T-C at sixty thousand ten, then zero point zero five B-T-C at sixty thousand fifteen. The sixty thousand thirty order is above the limit.

lines.text: Total cost: 3,000.50 plus 3,000.75, which is 6,001.25 USDT.
lines.say: Total cost: three thousand point five plus three thousand point seven five, which is six thousand one point two five U-S-D-T.

lines.text: Binance is one large crypto exchange. There are many others.
lines.say: Binance is one large crypto exchange. There are many others.

lines.text: The screens in this course are generic mocks, not real exchange screens.
lines.say: The screens in this course are generic mocks, not real exchange screens.

lines.text: Real apps change their labels over time, so check the app's own help pages.
lines.say: Real apps change their labels over time, so check the app's own help pages.

lines.text: Important: an exchange is not a bank.
lines.say: Important: an exchange is not a bank.

lines.text: Money you keep there is usually not protected the way a bank deposit is.
lines.say: Money you keep there is usually not protected the way a bank deposit is.

lines.text: Exchanges can pause withdrawals, get hacked, or even shut down.
lines.say: Exchanges can pause withdrawals, get hacked, or even shut down.

lines.text: And the rules differ from country to country.
lines.say: And the rules differ from country to country.

lines.text: Phishing is a fake message or website that tries to steal your login.
lines.say: Phishing is a fake message or website that tries to steal your login.

lines.text: Spot the red flags. Pressure: urgent, act now, or your account will be locked.
lines.say: Spot the red flags. Pressure: urgent, act now, or your account will be locked.

lines.text: A look-alike address with a small spelling change. And a request for your OTP.
lines.say: A look-alike address with a small spelling change. And a request for your O-T-P.

lines.text: Safer habits: type the address yourself or use a bookmark, and never share codes.
lines.say: Safer habits: type the address yourself or use a bookmark, and never share codes.

lines.text: Account security means keeping other people out of your account.
lines.say: Account security means keeping other people out of your account.

lines.text: Never share your password, your OTP codes, or API secret keys. Not with anyone.
lines.say: Never share your password, your O-T-P codes, or A-P-I secret keys. Not with anyone.

lines.text: Real support staff will never ask for them. Turn on two-step verification too.
lines.say: Real support staff will never ask for them. Turn on two-step verification too.

lines.text: Let's recap. An exchange runs a marketplace. Orders wait in the order book until prices meet.
lines.say: Let's recap. An exchange runs a marketplace. Orders wait in the order book until prices meet.

lines.text: Bid is the best buy price, ask the best sell price. The spread is ask minus bid.
lines.say: Bid is the best buy price, ask the best sell price. The spread is ask minus bid.

lines.text: An exchange is not a bank. Never share passwords, OTPs or API keys.
lines.say: An exchange is not a bank. Never share passwords, OTPs or A-P-I keys.

lines.text: Check yourself: best bid 59,990, best ask 60,010. What's the spread?
lines.say: Check yourself: best bid fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety, best ask sixty thousand ten. What's the spread?

lines.text: 60,010 minus 59,990 is 20 USDT.
lines.say: Sixty thousand ten minus fifty-nine thousand nine hundred ninety is twenty U-S-D-T.

lines.text: That's Phase 1! Next up: the Foundations Checkpoint, a short review of lessons one to four.
lines.say: That's Phase one! Next up: the Foundations Checkpoint, a short review of lessons one to four.
